## Natural history notes

A small tortricid moth characterized by yellowish to straw-colored forewings with brownish bands, speckling, and folded resting posture typical of leafroller moths. In Florida, it is found in gardens, orchards, fields, forest edges, parks, and other open or shrubby habitats where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed within rolled or tied leaves, flowers, or fruiting structures of a variety of plants, using silk shelters for protection as they develop.
